saints.name: St. Hilary of Arles
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A monk of Lérins raised young to the see of Arles, austere in life and famed for his eloquence…
biography: Born about 401 of a distinguished family in northern Gaul, Hilary seemed marked out for worldly honors when his kinsman Honoratus, founder of the abbey of Lérins, won him to the monastic life. He later told of the struggle between the Lord calling him and the world offering its charms.

When Honoratus, by then bishop of Arles, died in 429, Hilary succeeded him at about twenty-eight and presided over the councils of Orange and Vaison. He lived as a monk on the episcopal throne, going barefoot, working with his hands, and selling the vessels of the Church to ransom captives; his panegyric on his master, the Life of St. Honoratus, survives.

In 444 his zeal outran his jurisdiction: he deposed Chelidonius, bishop of Besançon, though Besançon lay in another province, and Pope Leo the Great reversed the sentence and stripped Hilary of his metropolitan powers. Hilary submitted, kept his see, and died at Arles on 5 May 449, not yet fifty; Leo himself praised his holiness.
saints.knownFor: His ascetic zeal and eloquent preaching as Bishop of Arles.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 5 May
